summary:
Japan’s December 7, 1941, surprise attack on Pearl Harbor was intended to disable the US Pacific Fleet while Japan expanded into Southeast Asia. After negotiations failed over Japan’s actions in China and Indochina, a Japanese carrier force launched 353 aircraft in two waves against the Hawaiian base.

The attack damaged all eight US battleships, sinking four, and destroyed more than 180 aircraft. It killed 2,403 Americans and wounded 1,178. Japan lost 29 aircraft, five midget submarines, and 130 personnel. The US carriers assigned to Pearl Harbor were at sea, and the attackers left the base’s oil storage and repair facilities intact.

Japan also launched coordinated attacks on US and British territories across the Pacific and Southeast Asia. The United States declared war on Japan on December 8; Germany and Italy declared war on the United States three days later, prompting US declarations of war against them. President Franklin D. Roosevelt called December 7 “a date which will live in infamy.”
